scoring: binary conjunction; all behavioral groups must pass

criteria.requirement: Aligned compatible warm cache eliminates backend requests and returns exactly the requested timestamps and values, including after repeated zoom changes.
Nondivisible and misaligned grids obtain correct fresh evaluations from downstream.
Reuse the covered prefix and fetch missing coverage without corrupting subsequent dense or coarse responses.
After partial fallback fetches a missing prefix, expanding the window returns the entire previously warm float tail and preserves dense responses.
The same partial-fallback window expansion preserves every native histogram timestamp and payload.
Tenant and partial-response semantics stay isolated across cache lookups.
Histogram timestamps and payloads survive subsampling and repeated cache reuse.
Valid empty cached ranges remain reusable.
Concurrent warm zoom-outs preserve results without unnecessary downstream requests.
Both sides of the daily query split preserve compatible reuse.
Independent metric-label maps and both labeled series survive compatible reuse.
Compatible reuse survives replacing the frontend process while retaining the configured remote cache.

An ordinary miss plus compatible-key lookup for one unsplit request to one cache server uses at most two actual remote retrieval commands. Check returned samples too. Count wire command frames, not Memcached cmd_get, which counts keys. No latency, exact key count, method-name or implementation-shape requirement.

fairness: No patch-text, symbol-name, exact key format, cache alternative ordering, or exact write-count requirements. Equivalent implementations can pass. Tests use immutable dependencies and real HTTP/process/cache boundaries. Binary scoring reflects a correctness-preserving cache feature; no partial reward for unsafe reuse.
